Data Crown Jewel Inventory & Data Flow Management
Data flows for all Data Crown Jewels must be documented, and the Data
Crown Jewel inventory as well as the associated Data Flow Registry
must be maintained and regularly updated.
Data flows for each Data Crown Jewel must be documented, maintained in
centralized Data Flow Registry●.
Data Crown Jewels4 are mission-critical data whose unauthorized disclosure
would cause intolerable and existential business impact. This includes but is
not limited to:
- Regulatory Impact: Severe regulatory consequences such as the
revocation of essential licenses or authorizations, making continued
business operations impossible.
- Financial Impact: Severe financial losses that threaten the
organization’s solvency or ability to continue operations.
- Customer and Market Trust Impact: Severe and sustained harmful
customer or market reaction, e.g. significant market movements that
threaten business viability.
- Operational Impact: Permanent or sustained disruption of critical core
services and operations that prevents the organization from
functioning
Asset-Types: Business Process

be reviewed at least annually to ensure completeness and ongoing
relevance●.

− RPO = 0 (Impact on Availability Criticality Level: “Critical”): Remote

− 0h < RPO < 1h (Impact on Availability Criticality Level: “Critical”):
Remote asynchronous replication for RPO < 1 hour but not 0 minutes
(e.g. RPO = 15, 20 or 30 minutes) and backup restore point and redo
logs + daily backup or alternative measures which guarantee no /
minimum data loss
− 1h ≤ RPO < 4h (Impact on Availability Criticality Level: “Major”): daily
backup (full or incremental) + every x hours during business hours redo
logs / snapshots / backups or alternative solution guaranteeing RPO
− 4 h ≤ RPO < 1 day (Impact on Availability Criticality Level: “Minor”):
daily backup (full or incremental) + every x hours during business
hours redo logs / snapshots / backups or alternative solution
guaranteeing RPO
− RPO of 1 day or more (Impact on Availability Criticality Level:
“Negligible”): weekly backup + daily (incremental) backups

col_2: AI Resource and Asset Management
Asset inventories of all AI Systems, General-purpose AI (GPAI) systems, AI
Models and AI Agents in development or in use must be maintained. Aside from
control requirements from ICT Asset Management additional attributes must be
maintained as defined in criteria below.
In addition to control requirements from ICT Asset Management, the dedicated or
centralized asset inventory must further include, at a minimum, the following
information for each AI Model:
− Model Provenance - The origin of the model i.e. In-house Developed, Third-
party Custom-developed, Open-source (Pre-trained), Commercial (Licensed)
− Training Data Lineage - A reference or link to the dataset(s) used for training,
fine-tuning, and testing the model.
− Data Sensitivity Profile - Classification of the training data, specifying if it
contained PII, market-sensitive, confidential and strictly confidential, or other
regulated information, even if the data was anonymized.
− AI platform – Information on the underlying Technology environment (platform)
used for AI lifecycle
− Model Architecture & Framework - The specific algorithm type and the software
framework/version used to build it
− Performance Metrics & Bias Assessment - A link to documentation containing
key performance metrics and the results of bias and fairness testing against
relevant protected attributes.
− Explainability (XAI) Method - The method used to explain the model's decisions,
if applicable.
In addition to control requirements from ICT Asset Management, the dedicated or
centralized asset inventory must further include, at a minimum, the following
information for each AI System incl. General-purpose AI (GPAI) system:
− AI Classification - The AI system's classification level, aligned with EU AI Act
tiers and ID 5 of this Guideline: (Prohibited AI practices; High-risk AI systems;
Systems with specific transparency obligations; Other AI systems).
− AI Use-Case – reference or link to AI Use case which is basis for the AI System
− AI platform – Information on the underlying Technology environment (platform)
used for AI lifecycle
− Intended Purpose & Prohibited Uses – A clear, unambiguous description of the
specific business task the system is approved for, and a list of explicitly
forbidden uses.
AI Awareness and Literacy Program
A comprehensive and role-specific AI literacy program must be established,
maintained, and continuously improved to ensure that all personnel involved in
the AI system lifecycle possess the necessary competence, awareness, and
understanding of AI-related risks, ethics, and operational responsibilities.
Transparency and Information on AI Systems
AI systems must provide clear, accessible, and comprehensive information to
enable deployers and users to understand, operate, and oversee the system
responsibly, ensuring transparency, interpretability, and compliance with the EU
AI Act and DBG frameworks.
Responsible and acceptable use of AI systems
Objectives for the responsible use of AI systems must be identified and
documented.
If acting as Provider, it must be ensured that documentation of High-risk AI systems
is transparent on design and development activities and enable Deployers to
interpret its output and appropriate use.

col_3: Right to Explanation
It must be ensured that affected individuals, subject to a decision which is taken
by the deployer based on the output from a high-risk AI system, receive clear and
meaningful explanations regarding the role of high-risk AI systems in decisions
that significantly impact them.
Explainability and Interpretability
The need and required degree of explanation for the AI system must be established,
documented, and communicated based on use-case criticality, audience, and
regulatory context.
The need and required degree for explanation of the AI system must be assessed
and documented.
A tailored explanation of why a particular output has been produced by the AI
system must be provided to the users of high-risk AI system with an explanation
method (Explainable AI).
Persons subject to a decision which is taken by the deployer on the basis of the
output from a high-risk AI System must be provided with explanations regarding the
role of a high-risk AI system in decisions that produce legal effects or significantly
affect them.

col_2: Classification of AI systems based on EU AI Act
All AI systems must be classified according to their AI risk level as defined by
the EU AI Act, and AI-related risks must be managed as an integral part of the
ICT Risk Management Framework through structured assessment, treatment,
and documentation processes.
Classification of General-Purpose AI Models
General-purpose AI models must be classified based on their capabilities and
impact, with specific thresholds and criteria determining whether they pose
systemic risk, requiring enhanced regulatory oversight under the EU AI Act.
Systems with Specific Transparency Obligations
AI systems subject to specific transparency obligations must clearly inform
natural persons when interacting with AI, disclose synthetic content generation,
and ensure compliance with disclosures made in a clear and timely manner.
AI Systems Risk Management
A comprehensive and lifecycle-wide risk management must be established for AI
systems, ensuring identification, assessment, treatment, documentation, and
monitoring of risks to health, safety, and fundamental rights, in alignment with
ICT Risk Management Policy and Guideline as well as EU AI Act requirements.

AI Risk management process
A comprehensive risk management process and procedure for AI systems and AI
models must be established, implemented, documented, and maintained throughout
their system lifecycle or the existing risk management processes and procedures
used.
Processes and procedures for management of AI risks must align with the ICT Risk
Management Policy and Guideline
Specific AI Risk management requirements
Before concluding a contract with a third-party service provider, a risk assessment
of the AI system must be carried out.
In the case of AI-specific subcontracting that supports critical or important functions
(CIF), the documented analysis must be performed to define:
− which third-parties are involved in data processing,
− location/region where this takes place and
− how long or complex chains of subcontracting may affect the process.
Besides control requirements from ICT Risk Management Guideline, specific risks
posed by AI systems must be identified and assessed throughout their lifecycle.
These include at least risks related to:
Health, safety, Fundamental rights
Data risks (e.g. Data security, integrity, privacy),
Model risks (e.g. Adversarial attacks, Prompt injections, Model interpretability,
Supply chain attacks)
Operational risks (e.g. Lack of accountability, Security Vulnerabilities, model drift)
Ethical and legal risks (e.g. Bias, fairness, Lack of explainability, transparency,
Intellectual property infringement
Misinformation (Hallucinations) and manipulation
The behavior of the AI system for inputs that do not conform to specified
requirements must be analyzed and documented using appropriate methods.
The risk assessment process for AI Systems, AI Models, AI Agents must include the
evaluation of potential consequences for individuals, groups, and society.
The risk assessment of high-risk AI Systems must include data from post-market
monitoring systems as defined in control requirement ID28 Post-Market Monitoring
System.
Human Oversight of AI Systems
AI systems must be designed and operated with appropriate human oversight
measures, based on criticality, that enable effective intervention, control, and/or
accountability, minimizing risks to health, safety, and fundamental rights.

Processes and procedures to ensure human oversight and control of the AI system
in compliance with regulatory requirements and organizational risk management
must be established.
Oversight Design and Implementation
The frequency, scope, and methods for security and robustness reviews of AI
models in production must be documented.
High-Risk AI systems must be designed and developed to include appropriate
human-machine interface tools that enable human intervention and control.
Critical decision points should be defined and integrated into AI related system
workflows, where Human-In-The-Loop is needed,
Every Human-In-The-Loop decision, approval, or override must be logged with
timestamps and user identifiers
The high-risk AI system must be monitored through human oversight throughout its
lifecycle.
Fundamental Rights Impact Assessment for High-Risk AI Systems
Before deploying high-risk AI systems for public services, a Fundamental Rights
Impact Assessment (FRIA) must be conducted and documented to evaluate
potential impacts on individuals’ fundamental rights. The results must be
submitted to the market surveillance authority using the official template
provided by the AI Office.
Applicability
Fundamental Rights Impact Assessment FRIA must be conducted prior to the first
use of a high-risk AI system when providing public services. AI systems listed under
Chapter 5.2. point 2 (critical infrastructure) are exempt from FRIA obligations.
AI Systems Data Governance
AI systems must be developed using training, validation, and testing datasets
that meet defined quality standards and are subject to robust data governance
practices, ensuring compliance with the EU AI Act, GDPR, and DBG Data
Governance frameworks.
AI Systems Technical Documentation
Comprehensive technical documentation must be created and maintained for
each AI system to demonstrate compliance with regulatory requirements,
covering design, development, testing, risk management, performance, and
lifecycle changes, and aligned with DBG’s Software Development and ICT
Change Management Guidelines.
AI Systems Events management and Logging
In addition to Control requirements from "Incident & Operational Event
Management Guideline”, for AI specific event records and logs must be
maintained throughout their lifecycle to ensure traceability, accountability, and
compliance with the EU AI Act, GDPR, and DBG’s Guidelines.
Accuracy, Robustness, and Access to AI Systems
AI systems must maintain accuracy, robustness, consistency and access
management throughout their lifecycle by implementing technical and
organizational measures to prevent, detect, and mitigate AI-specific
vulnerabilities, in alignment with ICT Risk Guidelines, EU AI Act, and DORA.
Secure AI System Development
Beside control requirements from “Software Development and ICT Change
Management Guideline” AI systems must follow additional development
practices throughout their lifecycle by implementing technical and organizational
measures.
AI Threat, Incident and Vulnerability Management
AI systems must implement robust cybersecurity measures to prevent, detect,
and respond to AI-specific threats, including adversarial manipulation and
input/output tampering. Beyond control requirements from ICT Patch and
Vulnerability Management Guideline further AI specific aspects must be
considered.
AI Agents Security and Boundaries
AI agents within AI systems must operate based on relevant established
processes for Agentic AI within DBG, within clearly defined and consistently
enforced security boundaries, tailored to roles, data confidentiality, and
operational environments.

col_3: Conformity assessment and Post-market monitoring for high-risk AI
Before placing a high-risk AI system in use, the appropriate conformity
assessment procedure must be followed, either with internal controls or via a
notified body, ensuring compliance with essential requirements through
verification of the quality management system, technical documentation, and
post-market monitoring processes.

Provider of high-risk AI System must establish the appropriate conformity
assessment procedure ensuring compliance with requirements for high-risk AI
systems from EU AI Act.
Conformity assessment based on internal control (Annex VI EU AI Act)
Conformity assessment procedure based on internal control for the high-risk AI
Systems must ensure that:
− AI System technical documentation (control requirement ID 12) is up to date,
− Compliance with all Requirements for high-risk AI Systems is regularly
assessed and results documented.
The provider must verify that the design and development process of the high-risk
AI system is consistent with the AI System technical documentation and document
at least the following aspects:
− risk management process used (control requirement ID 8),
− implementation and maintenance of a post-market monitoring system (control
requirement ID 28),
− procedures related to the reporting of a serious incident (control requirement
ID29)
Conformity based on assessment involving a notified body (Annex VII EU AI Act)
Where applicable, the DBG or LE acting as provider of high-risk AI system must
follow the conformity based on assessment involving a notified body, and create
application which must include at least:
− the name and address of the provider;
− the list of AI systems covered;
− the technical documentation for each AI system covered;
− the documentation covering all related internal control aspects listed in Chapter
5.6. of this Guideline;
− a written declaration that the same application has not been lodged with any
other notified body
Records of the notified body’s involvement and decisions must be retained and
made available to competent authorities upon request.

Key references

col_3: Documentation and Record-Keeping for high-risk AI
Documentation for high-risk AI systems must be securely stored and retained for
at least 10 years after market placement or as required by relevant EU financial
services laws. All records should be kept in a manner that ensures their integrity,
confidentiality, and accessibility, in line with ICT Risk and DBG Guidelines.
The following documentation must be retained for a minimum of 10 years after the
high-risk AI system is placed on the market or put into service, or in accordance with
applicable Union financial services law (where higher):
− Technical documentation (see control requirement ID 12 AI Systems Technical
Documentation).
− Documentation on internal control system for AI.
− Notified body approvals (where applicable).
− EU declarations of conformity (see control requirement ID 23 High-Risk AI
Systems Conformity Assessment).
All conformity assessment activities, including internal checks and third-party
evaluations, must be documented for high-risk AI system.
Records of high-risk AI systems must be retained in accordance with the ICT Risk
and other relevant DBG Guidelines and made available for audit or regulatory
review.
National competent authorities must be granted access to the retained
documentation upon request.
Documentation of AI system must be stored in a secure and accessible format,
ensuring integrity, confidentiality, and availability.

Corrective Actions for Non-Compliant high-risk AI systems
Corrective actions must be taken for non-compliant high-risk AI systems to
ensure regulatory compliance, including bringing the system into conformity,
disabling, withdrawing, or recalling it, and informing all relevant stakeholders.

Corrective Action Procedures
For any high-risk AI system found to be non-compliant, the Provider must take one
or more of the following corrective actions:
− Bring the system into conformity with applicable requirements.
− Disable the system to prevent further use.
− Withdraw the system from the market.
− Recall the system from users or deployers.
Stakeholder Notification
The Provider of high-risk AI system must inform Distributors and Deployers of the
provided AI system of the non-compliance and the corrective actions taken by the
Provider of a high-risk AI System.
If the high-risk AI system is considered to be a Product presenting a risk (to the
health or safety, or to fundamental rights, of persons), the Provider must investigate
the causes and inform the market surveillance authorities competent for the high-
risk AI system concerned.
All corrective actions for high-risk AI systems must be documented, including:
− The nature of non-compliance.
− The decision-making process for selecting the corrective action.
− The timeline and execution of the corrective measures.
− Communication records with stakeholders and authorities.
Integration with Incident Management
Corrective actions should be integrated into the DBG incident detection and
response processes, including AI-specific monitoring and escalation paths (see
control requirement ID 13 AI Systems Events management and Logging).
Logs and audit trails related to the AI incident and corrective actions must be
retained and reviewed.

Importer / Distributor Due Diligence for High-Risk AI Systems
If acting as Importer and/or Distributor due diligence must be performed to
ensure compliance with the EU AI Act before putting the AI Systems on the
market or making them available.

Importer Obligations
Importers must verify that high-risk AI systems comply with the EU AI Act before
placing them on the market.
The following elements must be checked by Importers of high-risk AI systems:
− Completion of the conformity assessment procedure (see control requirement ID
18 Conformity assessment and Post-market monitoring for high-risk AI)
− Availability and completeness of technical documentation (see control
requirement ID 12 AI Systems Technical Documentation).
− Presence of CE marking and EU declaration of conformity.
− Confirmation of authorized representation within the EU.
Where the high-risk AI system is considered to be a Product presenting a risk (to the
health or safety, or to fundamental rights, of persons), the Importer must inform the
Provider and the market surveillance authorities to that effect.
Distributor Obligations
Distributors must ensure that high-risk AI systems made available on the market
comply with the EU AI Act.
The following due diligence measures must be taken for high-risk AI system:
− Verification of provider markings and identification.
− Review of accompanying documentation and instructions for use.
− Confirmation that the system is not subject to corrective actions or restrictions
(see Control Requirement ID 20 Corrective Actions for Non-Compliant high-risk
AI systems).
Where the high-risk AI system is considered to be a Product presenting a risk (to the
health or safety, or to fundamental rights, of persons), the Distributor must inform
the Provider or Importer, and the authorities competent for the high-risk AI system to
that effect.

col_2: Provider Responsibilities in Value Chain and Intellectual Property
Legal entities assuming provider responsibilities for high-risk AI systems
through value chain activities, such as substantial modification, rebranding, or
integration, must ensure full compliance with the Third-Party ICT Risk
Management Guideline, EU AI Act, supported by written agreements with third-
parties that respect intellectual property and confidentiality obligations.
High-Risk AI Systems Conformity Assessment
High-risk AI systems must undergo a conformity assessment before being
placed on the market or put into service, ensuring compliance with the EU AI Act
through internal control or notified body procedures, with documentation
retained and accessible for regulatory oversight.

Assessment Procedure Selection
The appropriate conformity assessment procedure must be followed before placing
a high-risk AI system on the market or putting it into service.
− For AI systems listed under points 2 to 8 of Chapter 5.2 of this Guideline, the
internal control procedure (see control requirement ID 18 Conformity
assessment and Post-market monitoring for high-risk AI), should be used.
− For remote biometric identification, biometric categorization, and emotion
recognition systems, assessment by a notified body must be conducted.
Substantial Modifications
A new conformity assessment must be conducted if the high-risk AI system
undergoes substantial modifications that affect compliance with essential
requirements.
EU Declaration of Conformity
A signed EU declaration of conformity must be drawn up for each high-risk AI
system.
The EU declaration of conformity of a high-risk AI system must be retained for 10
years and provided to authorities upon request.
The EU declaration of conformity of high-risk AI system must include:
1. AI system name, type, and traceability reference.
2. Provider’s name and address.
3. Statement of sole responsibility.
High-Risk AI System Information for Registration
Detailed and up-to-date information about high-risk AI systems must be
submitted to the EU database prior to market placement or deployment.
Notification for General-Purpose AI with Systemic Risk
If a general-purpose AI model meets the criteria for systemic risk, the European
Commission must be notified within two weeks, including supporting evidence
and, if applicable, reasoned arguments for exemption. Designation by the
Commission must be complied with, and reassessment may be requested after
six months.
Obligations as Providers of General-Purpose AI Models (incl. systemic risk)
Providers of general-purpose AI models must maintain detailed technical
documentation, share essential information with downstream providers, comply
with copyright law, and publish a training data summary, in accordance with the
EU AI Act and templates provided by the AI Office.
Real-World Testing of High-Risk AI Systems
Real-world testing of high-risk AI systems must be conducted under strict
conditions, with informed consent, incident response protocols, and registration
in the EU database, ensuring transparency, safety, and regulatory compliance.
Serious Incident Reporting Procedure
A formal procedure must be established for reporting serious incidents related to
high-risk AI systems to market surveillance authorities and, where applicable,
notified bodies, ensuring timely notification, investigation, and corrective action
in compliance with the EU AI Act.
Post-Market Monitoring System
A proportionate post-market monitoring system must be established and
maintained for high-risk AI systems to ensure continuous compliance with the
EU AI Act and internal control requirements, through structured data collection,
performance analysis, and corrective action mechanisms.

System Establishment and Scope
A post-market monitoring system must be established and maintained for each high-
risk AI system.
The post-market monitoring system must be proportionate to the nature, risks, and
complexity of the AI system and should be integrated into existing systems,
provided equivalent protection is ensured.
Monitoring Plan and Documentation
The monitoring system must be based on a documented plan included in the
technical documentation of high-risk AI system (see control requirement ID 12 AI
Systems Technical Documentation) and must specify:
− Data sources and types.
− Collection methods and frequency.
− Analysis procedures and performance metrics.
− Corrective action mechanisms and escalation paths.
Performance Monitoring
The performance of the AI system must be continuously monitored and documented
using defined Key Performance Indicators (KPIs).
Performance requirements and KPIs should be included in the system description.
Deviations from defined performance thresholds of AI system must be made
transparent and addressed.
Data Collection and Analysis
The Post-Market Monitoring System for AI system must actively collect, document,
and analyze:
− Operational data from the AI system.
− Feedback and usage data from deployers.
− Interactions with other AI systems throughout the lifecycle.

col_3: Market Surveillance authorities and Non-Compliance
The full cooperation with market surveillance authorities must be ensured by
providing access to documentation, data, and other relevant artifacts necessary.
Corrective actions must be implemented when notified of non-compliance in
high-risk AI systems by market surveillance authorities.
Market surveillance authorities (relevant financial supervisory authority or another
relevant authority as identified by the Member State) must be granted full access to
the documentation as well as the training, validation and testing data sets used for
the development of high-risk AI systems
Market surveillance authorities must be cooperated with, and they must be provided
with necessary information, documentation, data sets, and source code (under
specific conditions) to facilitate their assessment of high-risk AI systems.
As an Operator, corrective action must be taken when national market surveillance
authorities identify and report risks related to high-risk AI systems, including its
withdrawal or recall if necessary.
All appropriate corrective actions must be taken to bring the AI system into
compliance:
− to withdraw the AI system from the market, or
− to recall it within a period the market surveillance authority may prescribe
Corrective actions must be implemented across the Legal Entities in EU market
when notified by a market surveillance authority about non-compliant high-risk AI
within the timeline prescribed.

col_2: The following AI practices must be prohibited (Article 5 EU AI Act)
Intended to use subliminal techniques outside of a person’s awareness to influence
a person’s behavior or purposefully manipulative or deceptive techniques, with the
effect of materially distorting behavior or appreciably impairing decision-making and
causing or be reasonably likely to cause significant harm;
Intended to exploit any of the vulnerabilities of a person or a specific group of
persons due to their age, disability or a specific social or economic situation, with
the objective to or the effect of materially distorting the behavior of that person or a
person pertaining to that group in a manner that causes or is reasonably likely to
cause that person or another person significant harm
Biometric categorization system that categorizes natural persons according to
sensitive or protected attributes or characteristics or based on the inference of those
attributes or characteristics;
Intended to be used for social scoring evaluation or classification of the
trustworthiness of individuals over time natural persons or groups thereof based on
their social behavior or known, inferred, or predicted personality characteristics
which may lead to a detrimental or unfavorable treatment either unrelated (to the
data generation/collection context) or unjustified/disproportionate (to the social
behavior);of such persons or groups thereof
Intended to be used for real-time biometric recognition in publicly accessible spaces
for purposes of law enforcement.
To be used for risk assessments of natural persons or groups thereof to assess the
risk of a natural person for offending or reoffending or for predicting the occurrence
or reoccurrence of an actual or potential criminal or administrative offence based on
profiling of a natural person or on assessing personality traits and characteristics;
To be used to create or expand facial recognition databases through the untargeted
scraping of facial images from the internet or CCTV footage
To be used to infer emotions of a natural person in the workplace or education
institutions.
High-risk AI systems are the AI systems listed in any of the following areas
(based on Article 6 (2) EU AI Act; ANNEX III):
Biometrics, in so far as their use is permitted under relevant Union or national law:
a) remote biometric identification systems.
b) This should not include AI systems intended to be used for biometric
verification the sole purpose of which is to confirm that a specific natural
person is the person he or she claims to be;
c) AI systems intended to be used for biometric categorization, according to
sensitive or protected attributes or characteristics based on the inference of
those attributes or characteristics
d) AI systems intended to be used for emotion recognition.
Critical infrastructure: AI systems intended to be used as safety components in the
management and operation of critical digital infrastructure, road traffic, or in the
supply of water, gas, heating or electricity.
Education and vocational training:
a) AI systems intended to be used to determine access or admission or to
assign natural persons to educational and vocational training institutions at
all levels;
b) AI systems intended to be used to evaluate learning outcomes, including
when those outcomes are used to steer the learning process of natural
persons in educational and vocational training institutions at all levels;
c) AI systems intended to be used for the purpose of assessing the appropriate
level of education that an individual will receive or will be able to access, in
the context of or within educational and vocational training institutions at all

d) AI systems intended to be used for monitoring and detecting prohibited

Employment, workers’ management and access to self-employment:

b) AI systems intended to be used to make decisions affecting terms of work-

contractual relationships, to allocate tasks based on individual behavior or
personal traits or characteristics or to monitor and evaluate the performance
and behavior of persons in such relationships.
Access to and enjoyment of essential private services and essential public services
and benefits:
a) AI systems intended to be used by public authorities or on behalf of public
authorities to evaluate the eligibility of natural persons for essential public
Information to be submitted upon the registration of high-risk AI systems in
accordance with Article 49 and Annex VIII EU AI Act
a) The following information must be submitted by providers to the EU
database prior to placing a high-risk AI system on the market:
1. Provider’s name, address, and contact details.
2. Contact details of any person submitting information on behalf of the
provider.
3. Authorized representative’s contact details (if applicable).
4. AI system trade name and traceability reference.
5. Description of the intended purpose and supported
components/functions.
6. Concise description of data used and operating logic.
7. System status (e.g., on market, recalled).
8. Certificate details from notified body (type, number, expiry date, body
ID).
9. Scanned copy of the certificate (if applicable).
10. Member States where the system is placed on the market or in service.
11. Copy of the EU declaration of conformity (see control requirement ID 23
High-Risk AI Systems Conformity Assessment).
12. Electronic instructions for use
13. 13. Optional URL for additional information.
b) The following information must be submitted by providers to the EU
database prior to placing a non-high-risk AI system on the market:
1. Provider’s contact details.
2. Contact details of any person submitting on behalf of the provider.
For the testing of high-risk AI systems in real world conditions outside AI
regulatory sandboxes all the following conditions must be met according to
Article 60 (4) EU AI Act
Testing Plan of high-risk AI system
− A real-world testing plan must be prepared and submitted to the competent
market surveillance authority in the Member State where testing will occur.
Approval of high-risk AI system
− Approval from the market surveillance authority must be obtained before testing
begins. Where tacit approval is permitted under national law, testing must not
commence until the approval period has elapsed.
Registration of high-risk AI system
− Testing in real-world conditions must be registered with a unique Union-wide
identification number and include all information specified in Annex IX EU AI Act.
− For AI systems in sensitive areas (law enforcement, migration, asylum, border
control), registration must be completed in the secure non-public EU database as
required by Article 49 EU AI Act.
Legal Representation related to high-risk AI system
− The provider or prospective provider must be established in the Union or must
appoint a legal representative established in the Union.
Data Transfer and Protection (high-risk AI system)
− Data collected during testing must not be transferred to third countries unless
appropriate safeguards under Union law are implemented.
− Personal data of test subjects must be deleted after testing is completed.
According to Annex IX EU AI Act, the following information must be provided and
thereafter kept up to date regarding testing of high-risk AI systems in real-world
conditions to be registered in accordance with Article 60 EU AI Act:
According to Annex IX EU AI Act, the following information must be provided and
thereafter kept up to date regarding testing of high-risk AI systems in real-world
conditions to be registered in accordance with Article 60 EU AI Act:
1. A Union-wide unique single identification number of the testing in real world
conditions;
2. The name and contact details of the provider or prospective provider and of
the deployers involved in the testing in real world conditions;
3. A brief description of the AI system, its intended purpose, and other
information necessary for the identification of the system;
4. A summary of the main characteristics of the plan for testing in real world
conditions;
5. Information on the suspension or termination of the testing in real world
conditions.
These requirements (according to Annex VII EU AI Act) apply to high-risk AI
systems that undergo a conformity assessment based on a quality management
system and technical documentation review by a notified body.
An approved internal control system for AI for the design, development, and testing
of high-risk AI systems must be established, examined, and maintained in
accordance with regulatory requirements.
The technical documentation for each high-risk AI system must be compiled and
examined for conformity by a notified body.
A complete set of documentation for the internal control system for AI (AI ICS) must
be created and maintained. This documentation must include:
− The name and address of the provider and any authorized representatives.
− A definitive list of all AI systems covered by the AI ICS.
− The complete technical documentation for each listed AI system.
− Detailed documentation of the AI ICS, covering all aspects required by Article 17 of
the EU AI Act.
− A description of the procedures in place to ensure the AI ICS remains adequate
and effective.
− A written declaration confirming that the same application has not been lodged with
another notified body.
The approved AI ICS must be continuously implemented and maintained to ensure
its adequacy and effectiveness.
Any intended changes to the approved AI ICS or the list of AI systems it covers
must be identified, documented, and communicated to the relevant notified body for
assessment.
All assessment decisions, conclusions, and notifications from the notified body
